title: Micro-batching & KV cache edge-case retro — 2025-04-21
body:
Meeting: Micro-batching & KV cache edge-case retrospective
Date: 2025-04-21
Location: Zoom + huddle room B
Attendees: Jordan Kim (owner), Aisha Patel, Carlos Mendes, Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor, notes by Jordan

Purpose: Capture the root cause and mitigation plan for intermittent p99 latency spikes observed in long-context generation workloads (mostly customer A and internal load tests), and agree on safe short-term mitigations and longer-term kernel/runtime changes. This doc is intentionally informal and focused on action items and reproducibility notes.

1) Quick summary
- Symptom: recurring p99 bursts (~600-900 ms increase) under sustained long-context workloads (context lengths 8k-16k tokens) starting sprint 23. Not constant — happens in 1-2% of requests but impacts SLAs.
- Initial suspect: batching heuristics (micro-batching thresholds) interacting badly with KV cache lookups and kernel scheduling heavy-tail lock contention.
- Current status: have a minimal mitigation (temporarily increasing micro-batch flush time and turning on aggressive KV cache prefetch) that reduces incidence but increases average latency ~20 ms. Plan: iterative fixes + a conservative rollout.

2) Timeline & how we found it
- 2025-04-10: Customer A reports p99 spikes during a product launch.
- 2025-04-12: Internal loadtest reproduces spikes on our canary pool.
- 2025-04-14: Team triage: observed correlation with workloads that have variable sequence lengths and many mid-query cache accesses.
- 2025-04-16: Kernel tracing + eBPF snapshots show periodic kernel-side scheduling delays where worker threads spend repeated short periods (50-200ms) contending on the KV cache LRU list mutex.
- 2025-04-18: Experimented with micro-batch thresholds (4,8,16) and found tradeoffs: lower thresholds reduce tail at cost of throughput.

3) Repro recipe (internal)
- Steps to reproduce locally on canary: run loadtest script 'tests/load/long_context_spike.py' with --seq-len 12000, --qps 250, and enable 'mix-varying-prefixes' dataset. Spike appears within 3-10 minutes.
- Required flags: --batch-window-ms 6 --kv-cache=on --kv-eviction-policy=lru
- Observed artifacts: repeated cache misses for fragmented prefix keys (we call this 'prefix-fragmentation') and a burst of small micro-batches causing many concurrent KV lookups that serialize on the LRU list.

4) Investigation notes & hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: micro-batching bursts create many small concurrent KV lookups; the KV cache implementation serializes updates to the LRU metadata, causing lock contention.
- Hypothesis B: our kernel scheduling (thread priorities) allows background housekeeping threads to preempt worker threads during short windows, amplifying latency when micro-batches cluster.
- Hypothesis C: prefix-fragmentation causes higher-than-expected cache churn; many small keys that should be coalesced are stored separately due to suffix hashing mismatch introduced by quantization alignment changes.
- Evidence: flame graphs show dominant time in kv_cache::touch_lru for p99 requests, and perf counters show increased syscalls around futex waits; PR 1623 addresses some LRU thin-locks but doesn't fully remove contention.

5) Measurements (canary results)
- Baseline (no mitigation): p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=420-530ms (bursty) at 250 qps, seq=12k
- Mitigation 1 (increase batch-window-ms from 6->12): p50=48ms, p95=130ms, p99=210-260ms (reduced spikes but slightly higher median)
- Mitigation 2 (enable aggressive prefetch + kv_prefetch_threads=4): p50=50ms, p95=125ms, p99=190-230ms
- Mitigation combined: p50=52ms, p95=135ms, p99=160-180ms, throughput down ~6%
- Kernel-change experiment (local patch to adaptive LRU thin-lock): p50=46ms, p95=122ms, p99=145-160ms without throughput regression (promising, needs stress testing)

6) Root cause (current best explanation)
- Interaction of three factors: (1) micro-batches producing many concurrent small KV lookups; (2) KV cache LRU metadata serialized by a thin lock leading to short heavy contention windows; (3) kernel scheduling preemption making those small windows longer (coordinated effect produces observable p99 spikes). Prefix fragmentation increases frequency of LRU updates.

7) Proposed short-term mitigations (safe, rollout in canary first)
- S1 (immediate, infra change): Increase micro-batch flush window from 6ms to 12ms for canary pools. Rationale: reduce number of micro-batches that land concurrently. Cost: slight median increase. Owner: Priya (rollout script). Target: 2025-04-23.
- S2: Enable kv_prefetch with 4 threads (config): warms hot prefix entries reducing LRU churn. Owner: Aisha. Target: 2025-04-23.
- S3: Canary diagnostic flags to collect per-request kv-touch counts and LRU wait timing (adds metrics to console). Owner: Jordan. Target: 2025-04-22.

8) Proposed medium-term engineering fixes
- M1: Replace single LRU thin-lock with sharded LRU buckets by key-hash. Low-risk refactor; expected to reduce contention proportionally to shard count. Owner: Carlos. Target: prototype by 2025-05-07.
- M2: Kernel scheduling guard: mark worker threads as SCHED_BATCH for short critical sections or use pthread_priority bump during kv-touch (experiment). Owner: Liam. Target: feasibility doc by 2025-05-01.
- M3: Batch coalescing logic: smarter coalescing to avoid bursts — use token-length aware window and prefix-awareness so requests likely to touch similar prefixes are coalesced. Owner: Priya + Carlos. Target: design doc by 2025-05-05.
- M4: Storage layout fix for prefix-fragmentation: ensure canonical prefix canonicalization prior to key insertion to avoid redundant keys (affects serialization/hot-key detection). Owner: Aisha. Target: spike PR by 2025-05-09.

9) Experiments to run (priority order)
- E1: Sharded LRU prototype on canary with synthetic workload; measure p99 and throughput for shard counts [4,8,16]. (Carlos)
- E2: Adaptive micro-batch flush: dynamic window that grows when kv-touch rate is high. (Priya)
- E3: Kernel thread priority bump microbenchmark; cannot roll to prod without perf team signoff. (Liam)
- E4: Key canonicalization A/B test to verify reduction in kv-touch rates and LRU ops. (Aisha)

10) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Jordan: deploy canary diagnostic flags and dashboards (2025-04-22)
- Priya: rollout increased batch-window to 12ms on canary and monitor (2025-04-23)
- Aisha: open spike PR for key canonicalization and schedule review (2025-04-28)
- Carlos: prototype sharded LRU and share perf numbers (2025-05-07)
- Liam: write feasibility doc for thread-priority approach and potential risks (2025-05-01)
- All: daily sync (15 min) for the next week at 10:15am PT to monitor canary and adjust mitigations

11) Risks and tradeoffs
- Increasing batch window reduces burst tail but increases median latency and modestly reduces qps; visible to latency-sensitive customers.
- Sharded LRU increases memory overhead and complexity in eviction policies. Need careful instrumentation.
- Thread-priority tricks could interact poorly with multi-tenant kernel settings in our shared clouds; must coordinate with infra.

12) Open questions
- What is the long-term desired behavior for hot-prefix coalescing across requests from different tenants? (product question)
- Can we expose a configuration knob per-customer for batch-window and kv-prefetch? (business/devops question)

13) Notes to self / next sync agenda
- Collect histograms of kv-touch counts per request and top 20 hot prefixes.
- Validate that PR 1623 reduces but doesn't eliminate lock paths.
- Review canary metrics after S1+S2 by 2025-04-24 and prepare rollback plan.

Appendix: quick links
- Jira: INF-4823 (incident), INF-4839 (LRU sharding epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1623 (thin-lock reductions)
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1640000000000

End of notes. This doc should be a working artifact; update as experiments land.
